title: QuantumMed POC: private networking benchmarks & SLO scoping
summary: POC scoping to validate Private networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink) and data residency constraints for a production Redwood Private pilot. Agreed success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput, security checklist), workload sizing (RPS, token distribution), and a three-week benchmark/timeline. Action items: exchange network diagrams, security questionnaire, run initial micro-benchmarks next week, schedule in-VPC load test.
next_steps: Redwood to send detailed network diagram + Private deployment checklist (Maya)
QuantumMed to share internal VPC CIDR and existing peering/request form (Marco)
Redwood SE to publish micro-benchmark script and instructions for in-VPC run (Ethan)
Priya to validate KMS/HSM and provide compliance contacts; confirm SOC2 scope (Priya)
Schedule in-VPC 24h soak test week of 2026-11-16 (tentative)
action_items: Maya Patel: send Private deployment checklist and security pack (due 2026-11-04)
Ethan Cole: share load-generator scripts and sample Terraform for PrivateLink endpoint (due 2026-11-05)
Marco Diaz: provide VPC CIDR, peering/privatelink requester and current NAT/egress rules (due 2026-11-06)
Priya Singh: confirm KMS/HSM footprint and SOC2 audit contacts (due 2026-11-06)
Oliver Wang: finalize success criteria doc with product SLAs (due 2026-11-09)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-02 15:30 PT — duration ~48m. Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (CTO), Marco (SRE), Priya (Compliance), Oliver (Product)

00:00 Maya: ok uh thanks everyone for making time, we know you wanted to focus on the private networking side and the benchmark plan today. quick intros?
00:07 Lena: hey uh Lena Ortiz CTO at QuantumMed, thanks. we're trying to lock down residency and make sure nothing leaves our VPC, basically.
00:14 Marco: Marco Diaz, infra. we'll own the peering/privatelink setup. we have strict egress firewall rules and hairpinning is a no-go.
00:20 Priya: Priya Singh, compliance. SOC2 stuff, KMS, audit logs — we'll want to validate everything.
00:25 Maya: perfect. Ethan from our SE team will lead the bench and the networking tradeoffs. Ethan?
00:31 Ethan: hi all. quick overview: there's two common architectures — VPC peering, which gives you direct route-level access, and PrivateLink, which exposes an interface endpoint and keeps traffic scoped. each has tradeoffs for routing, egress and when you need cross-account.
00:42 Marco: can you say more about egress? our policy disallows any outbound internet from private subnets — only via approved NAT gateways and proxy.
00:48 Ethan: yeah so with peering traffic stays in the AZ/VPC route tables, nothing needs an internet hop. with PrivateLink the interface endpoint initiates connections to our service backplane, but you still need to ensure your endpoint doesn't have a path that allows unintended internet egress. sometimes customers attach endpoint to private subnets that route via a proxy and that can leak if misconfigured, so we usually advise explicit route table entries and NACLs.
01:10 Lena: so peering is simpler for us?
01:12 Ethan: often yes for raw east-west latency and avoiding extra hops. PrivateLink is slightly more controlled for least-privilege cross-account access and can help with audit isolation. but PrivateLink can complicate some use cases like mTLS to your own backends unless you front it correctly.
01:29 Marco: what about IP limits? we have strict CIDR planning.
01:33 Ethan: peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs; PrivateLink works across overlapping CIDRs because you use an ENI. important to check your available /24s for endpoints.
01:45 Oliver: ok, on the POC we want to validate two things: one, that latency meets our SLOs for interactive features; two, that data never leaves our jurisdiction for the EU pilot.
01:55 Maya: can you state the success criteria you have in mind?
01:58 Oliver: p50 <60ms, p95 <200ms for typical chat flows, throughput of 30 qps steady-state for the summarization pipeline, plus audit logs and KMS integration verified.
02:11 Priya: also need data residency proof (no egress to other regions) and proof that logs are retained per our policy.
02:18 Ethan: noted. to scope benchmarks we need workload details: tokens per request, typical prompt/response sizes, distribution of short vs long sequences, and concurrency patterns.
02:28 Marco: our retrieval-augmented workload has average prompt 380 tokens, avg response 620 tokens, with 65% of calls under 1k tokens. Peak bursts up to 200 concurrent sessions for a small user group.
02:41 Ethan: great, that's very helpful. that maps to roughly X tokens per second — we estimate 30 qps * 1000 tokens = 30k tokens/sec, which will influence batching and GPU selection.
02:54 Lena: we also want to test cold starts — the first request after model cache eviction.
02:58 Ethan: yes we will include cold-start percentile in the plan. we'll run cold start, steady-state, and long soak with KV/prefix cache warm up to measure degradation/regrowth.
03:10 Oliver: what about quantization — do you recommend a quantized variant for the POC?
03:13 Ethan: we can run both float32 and int8-like quantized profiles; quantization reduces memory and can increase throughput but may change output quality. for the POC we'll do a quality check on a fixed eval set as part of the plan.
03:24 Marco: timeline?
03:26 Maya: proposed timeline: this week exchange network diagrams and IAM roles; next week (week of 11/09) initial micro-benchmarks from Redwood inside our test VPC; week of 11/16 run a 24h soak and peak burst tests; week of 11/23 evaluate results and decide whether to extend to dedicated capacity.
03:43 Priya: sounds aggressive but workable. Compliance will need the security pack asap.
03:47 Maya: we'll send that today, plus a Private deployment checklist.
03:50 Ethan: for the micro-benchmarks we'll provide a load generator (k6 + custom token generator) and a sample Terraform to create interface endpoints if you choose PrivateLink.
03:59 Marco: do you need audit log access or will you push logs to our S3?
04:03 Ethan: we can ship logs to your S3 via an encrypted delivery, or we can give you a read-only export. for SOC2 proof we'll provide timestamps and request IDs, and we can integrate with your SIEM via a secure endpoint.
04:15 Priya: KMS — we need to ensure keys are customer-managed and HSM-backed. does Redwood support using our KMS/HSM?
04:22 Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys and HSM integrations; we'll include the KMS integration doc.
04:27 Marco: any constraints around region lockdown? we need the cluster to be pinned to us-east-1 and eu-central-1 for the other project.
04:34 Ethan: region pinning is supported. for EU residency we can provision a separate Private deployment in eu-central-1 and disable cross-region failover for the POC.
04:43 Oliver: ok, competition question — we ran some internal infra tests against our own GPU fleet and saw similar throughput but higher tail latency. we're curious how Redwood's caching helps.
04:51 Ethan: our platform uses automatic KV/prefix caching and continuous batching; for many RAG flows this reduces per-token work and improves p95 significantly once warmed. the benchmark will measure cold vs warmed cache.
05:03 Lena: what exactly do you need from us to start the micro-benchmark inside our VPC?
05:08 Ethan: 1) VPC CIDR and subnets to create endpoints or peering; 2) IAM role or cross-account role for endpoint creation if using PrivateLink; 3) a test subnet with NAT disabled (to ensure no unintended egress) and sample security group rules; 4) point of contact for network changes (Marco).
05:25 Marco: we can provide that. will you need any open ports?
05:28 Ethan: only outbound to our service on TLS 443 if PrivateLink; for peering you'll use normal TCP routes to the instance IPs — we'll give exact port ranges in the network doc.
05:39 Maya: let's clarify success criteria now to make sure the POC sign-off is unambiguous. Oliver, you mentioned p95 <200ms — any tolerances?
05:48 Oliver: if p95 breaches 200ms more than 5% of requests in steady-state, fail. p50 target 60ms, and accuracy regression under 2% on the eval set. security items must be green.
06:01 Priya: we also need proof that logs cannot be exfiltrated and that access is auditable.
06:06 Ethan: we'll add a detailed checklist itemizing audit trails, key rotation, and export controls.
06:13 Maya: OK cool. final questions?
06:15 Lena: what's the rollback if something leaks during the test?
06:18 Ethan: we will run tests in a dedicated test VPC and only use read-only test data. if anything unexpected is observed we have a kill switch to sever the link and rotate any test keys.
06:27 Marco: for the soak test, what metrics will you collect?
06:30 Ethan: latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and network egress bytes. we'll provide dashboards and raw CSVs.
06:41 Oliver: good. can you include cost estimates for running at 30 qps steady-state vs dedicated?
06:46 Maya: yes we'll include a cost model with per-token baseline and dedicated commit estimate.
06:52 Maya: awesome — thanks everyone. recap of next steps: Maya send security pack, Ethan share bench scripts, Marco share VPC info, Priya confirm keys. we'll target bench start week of Nov 9.
07:05 Lena: thanks, talk soon.
07:07 Maya: thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
